steps: Choose the correct formula (given on the formula sheet for cones, spheres, pyramids)
Substitute measurements carefully (radius vs diameter, perpendicular height vs slant)
Calculate and give correct units (cm³ for volume, cm² for surface area)
method_card.title: Volume & Surface Area
method_card.content:
Prisms: Volume = area of cross-section × length. Cuboid: V = \(lwh\), SA = \(2(lw + lh + wh)\). Cylinder: V = \(\pi r^2 h\), SA = \(2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh\).

Pyramid: V = \(\frac{1}{3} \times\) base area \(\times h\). Cone: V = \(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\), Curved SA = \(\pi r l\) (\(l\) = slant height). Sphere: V = \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\), SA = \(4\pi r^2\).
method_card.example:
Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 4 cm and height 10 cm.

\(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi \times 16 \times 10 = 160\pi \approx 502.7\) cm³

gold.display: A cone has radius 3 cm and slant height 5 cm. Find the total surface area to 1 d.p.

misconceptions.message: Total SA = πrl + πr² = π×3×5 + π×9 = 15π + 9π = 24π = 75.4 cm².
Total surface area includes the base (πr²) as well as the curved surface (πrl).

gold.display: A frustum is formed by removing a small cone (r=2, h=3) from a large cone (r=6, h=9). Find the volume of the frustum to 1 d.p.

misconceptions.message: Large cone: ⅓π(36)(9) = 108π. Small cone: ⅓π(4)(3) = 4π. Frustum = 108π − 4π = 104π = 326.7 cm³.

gold.display: A sphere fits exactly inside a cylinder. The sphere has radius 5 cm. Find the volume of the empty space inside the cylinder. Give your answer to 1 d.p.
A solid is a cylinder (r=4 cm, h=10 cm) with a hemisphere (r=4 cm) on top. Find the total volume to 1 d.p.
A sphere has surface area \(100\pi\) cm². Find the radius.

bronze.display: Find the volume of a cuboid with length 6 cm, width 4 cm and height 3 cm.
Find the surface area of a cube with side length 5 cm.

misconceptions.message: That's the volume (5³). Surface area = 6 × 5² = 6 × 25 = 150 cm².

bronze.display: A triangular prism has a cross-section area of 12 cm² and length 10 cm. Find its volume.

misconceptions.message: Volume of a prism = cross-section area × length = 12 × 10 = 120 cm³.

bronze.display: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 7 cm. Give your answer to 1 d.p.

misconceptions.message: V = πr²h = π × 9 × 7 = 63π = 197.9 cm³. Make sure you use the radius, not diameter.

bronze.display: A cuboid has volume 180 cm³. Its length is 9 cm and width is 5 cm. Find the height.
Find the volume of a cube with side length 4 cm.
A cylinder has diameter 10 cm and height 6 cm. Find the volume to 1 d.p.
Find the surface area of a cuboid 8 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm.

silver.display: A cone has radius 5 cm and height 12 cm. Find the volume to 1 d.p.

misconceptions.message: V = ⅓πr²h = ⅓ × π × 25 × 12 = 100π = 314.2 cm³. Don't forget the ⅓.

silver.display: A sphere has radius 6 cm. Find the volume to 1 d.p.
A sphere has radius 4 cm. Find the surface area to 1 d.p.

misconceptions.message: SA = 4πr² = 4 × π × 16 = 64π = 201.1 cm². Don't confuse with volume.

silver.display: A cylinder has surface area 150π cm². Its radius is 5 cm. Find its height.
A pyramid has a square base of side 6 cm and height 10 cm. Find the volume.

misconceptions.message: V = ⅓ × base area × h = ⅓ × 36 × 10 = 120 cm³. Don't forget the ⅓.

silver.display: A hemisphere has radius 9 cm. Find its volume to 1 d.p.

misconceptions.message: Hemisphere = half sphere: V = ½ × (4/3)πr³ = (2/3) × π × 729 = 486π = 1526.8 cm³.

silver.display: A cone has volume 150π cm³ and radius 5 cm. Find the height.
